title: Non-Multiplicativity of the Holevo Barycenter of Quantum Channels
authors: Sayantan Chakraborty, Stefano Mancini, Leonardo Rossetti, Andreas Winter
abstract: The Holevo barycenter of a quantum channel is the unique output state obtained as the average output of any ensemble achieving the Holevo capacity. Given two quantum channels, the multiplicativity problem asks whether this barycenter tensorizes under parallel composition, namely whether the barycenter of the product channel coincides with the tensor product of the individual barycenters. This question is closely related to the additivity problem for the Holevo capacity: additivity implies tensorization of the Holevo barycenter, while tensorization alone is not sufficient for additivity. Although a construction is known that demonstrates the existence of channels with non-additive Holevo capacity, their corresponding Holevo barycenters still tensorize, leaving open whether multiplicativity might ultimately hold universally. Here, we answer this question in the negative by exhibiting channels for which the Holevo barycenter is not multiplicative under the tensor product of the channel with itself. Moreover, we show that the entropy of the Holevo barycenter is neither universally subadditive nor universally superadditive under tensor product.
summary: This paper tackles the multiplicativity problem for the Holevo barycenter of quantum channels, a concept related to the additivity of the Holevo capacity. The authors demonstrate that this barycenter is generally not multiplicative, providing explicit counterexamples. This result shows that the geometric structure of optimal quantum measurements is sensitive to the tensor product structure of the underlying channels.
main_problem: The paper investigates the multiplicativity problem for the Holevo barycenter of quantum channels, asking if the barycenter of a product channel equals the tensor product of the individual barycenters.
main_result:
The authors prove that the Holevo barycenter is generally not multiplicative, providing counterexamples where $\Omega(N \otimes N) 
eq \Omega(N) \otimes \Omega(N)$. They also show the entropy of the barycenter is neither universally subadditive nor superadditive.
method: The analysis involves constructing specific quantum channels using direct sums and tensor products, comparing derived block weights, and analyzing the von Neumann entropy of the output ensemble.
model_or_system: The study concerns general quantum channels $N: L(H) 	o L(K)$ acting on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, relating concepts like Holevo capacity and the Holevo barycenter.
key_observables: Holevo Capacity ($\chi(N)$), Holevo Barycenter ($\Omega(N)$), Von Neumann entropy of the output ensemble ($\mathcal{H}(\Omega)$), and Shannon entropies of associated probability distributions.
important_parameters: The analysis relies on constructing channels exhibiting superadditive Holevo capacity ($\chi(\mathcal{N}_1 \otimes \mathcal{N}_2) = \chi(\mathcal{N}_1) + \chi(\mathcal{N}_2) + \delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the relationship between additivity/multiplicativity and the barycenter, establishes formulas for direct-sum and tensor-product channels, and then constructs specific counterexamples to disprove universal multiplicativity.
why_interesting: This work delves into the fundamental structural properties of quantum information measures, showing that even when capacity fails to be additive, the associated geometric structure (the barycenter) can fail to be multiplicative, highlighting deep non-linearities in quantum resource theories.
